says: In today's tooling, the Runs service never says why it refused to move a folder's runs/. RunsFs answers one constant, { said: '', kept: false }, for a runs/ link, a runs/ file, MAIN's own runs/ and every failed write or move, so gc prints 'keep <name>: could not keep its runs/' and box rm 'kept box <name>' with no cause. keepruns.sh wrote the cause on stderr (not a plain folder, that is MAIN's own runs/, move failed), but RunsProcess (stderr: 'ignore') and gc's keepRuns (r.err unread) already dropped it, so the port did not lose a fact anyone read; it ported the script without the one place the reason was produced. AGENTS.md's data-shape rule names 'why something was refused' as a fact to record.
proof: RunsFs.ts:17 is 'const refused: Kept = { said: "", kept: false };' and line 74 maps every PlatformError to it; box/Runs.ts's Kept has only 'said' and 'kept'. The deleted keepruns.sh (git show bc66217) printed 'runs of $name: not a plain folder', 'that is MAIN's own runs/' and 'move failed' to stderr.
cost: A box that gc keeps forever because its runs/ cannot move (a link, a cross-device move now that rename replaces mv, a permission error) shows no reason; a person has to rerun the steps by hand to learn it.
